question.text: Sahyadri Stat-Arb enters at z = +2 (spread = INR 7.40) with INR 10 cr LONG in Stock Q and INR 10 cr SHORT in Stock P. Spread reverts to mean INR 5.00 (z=0). Assuming the INR 2.40 spread compression translates linearly to combined pair P&L of INR 2.40 lakh per INR 10 cr pair leg (illustrative), what is the GROSS P&L on the pair?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per the problem's linear assumption, spread compression from INR 7.40 to INR 5.00 = INR 2.40 move; pair P&L = INR 2.40 lakh. Both legs contribute (long cheap leg gains, short rich leg gains on the move toward mean). **The Trap:** Options misapply the conversion. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C similar. VIII tests pair P&L arithmetic. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Real pairs are not linear — there's Beta adjustment, dividend events, and basis. Backtest the pair's actual P&L per unit z-reversion over history; use empirical conversion rather than the notional formula. Charge 10-20 bps transaction cost per round-trip pair.
